answer: An optical-magnetic protocol curbs Sybil attacks by binding agent identities to physical coordinates. Candidate nodes direct a pulsed beam off a MEMS mirror to an anchor station while measuring inductive response against a nearby ferrous plate. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated physical hardware and securing distinct land per identity. However, line-of-sight occlusions from wildlife like a sparrow distort timing measurements, causing false attestation failures.
